text.p: - All Russians will be given a personal identification number in what is seen as a move to computerise the ailing system of tax collection and pension payments.
- Masked gunmen who last week murdered six Red Cross workers in a Chechen hospital came especially to look for them, says the paper, quoting witnesses.

- A delegation representing a number of European embassies in Moscow has visited the foreign ministry to protest at the new tax supposed to be levied at every crossing of the Russian border. The tax is likely to be introduced shortly.
- President Boris Yeltsin returns to the Kremlin after a long absence and promises to tackle social issues first.
- A woman working as an aide to three different deputies of the Federal Assembly was shot dead in her Moscow flat on Sunday.
- A "new" Yeltsin returns to the old Kremlin but it is still unclear whether any dramatic policy changes are to follow.
- Alexander Lebed seems ready to return to big politics.
- Kiev will be one of the first world capitals President Yeltsin is planning to visit.
- President Yeltsin returns to the Kremlin and a wave of sackings among top officials may be on the cards.
